C. EXECUTIVE AUTHORITY TO 
DIRECT AGENCY POLICY
Although patronage is not unimportant in poRtical life or in 
constitutional theory, the powers to appoint and to remove government 
officers represent only a portion of the stakes in the elected branches 
pohtical competition. The degree to which the president may influence or 
even dictate the decisions made pursuant to authority delegated by statute 
to others is, in many contexts, much more critical.
